name: inprocess-obi-apb-tlul-mixed-timer-rvtimer-f1f4
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches an APB3 register target and a TL-UL register target in one process: the PULP timer at 0x40001000 (the one F5 target) and the OpenTitan rv_timer at 0x40003000. Every target states its own protocol from its own artifact, the host samples each target's own trace (psel/penable/pready for APB3, the A/D channels for TL-UL), and each case states the protocol of the target it was routed to.
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex RVFI) reaches two independently addressed MMIO targets of different protocols in one process: target 0 is the PULP timer at 0x40001000 behind the real apb3_mmio_bridge (profile protocol apb/3), target 1 is the OpenTitan rv_timer at 0x40003000 behind the real beat_to_tlul adapter (profile protocol tl-ul/1).

The timer window is the profile's own 4 KiB APB3 window; the rv_timer window is its own 4 KiB TL-UL window. 0x40001000..0x40002000 and 0x40003000..0x40004000 do not overlap, neither overlaps the RAM image 0x10000..0x30000, and both clear the 4 GiB bound.

Timer registers: TIMER0_COUNT(0), TIMER0_CTRL(4), TIMER0_CMP(8), the same three the APB3 mixed pair uses. rv_timer registers used here: CTRL(0x4, rw) and COMPARE_LOWER0_0(0x118, rw), the two the homogeneous TL-UL scenario declares.

Only target 0 declares F5 facts, through configs/behaviors/pulp_timer_f5.json, so F5 remains one APB3 target's own window: irq_o[0], a 16-tick pulse, trigger writes [[4,0],[8,0],[0,4294967295]] and the TIMER0_COUNT status word at offset 0. The TL-UL target declares no behavior file, so it declares no F5 facts, is reached by F2/F4 only, and the summary states target1_f5 no. A TL-UL target that did declare the four facts would be admitted (F5_TARGET_PROTOCOLS contains tl-ul), but then the session would have two declaring targets and this scenario does not claim that shape.

The TL-UL target's own trace is sampled on its A and D channels: every F2/F4 case routed to it states tlul_a_valid/a_ready/a_opcode/a_address/a_mask/a_data and tlul_d_valid/d_ready/d_data/d_error from the slave's own pins, and completion is one A handshake followed by one D handshake.
No DMA is declared: the route criterion is the APB3 one, and this scenario claims no DMA-to-target route. F6 is therefore refused as unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:APB3+TL-UL.
Both profiles declare 50 MHz, so one host tick drives all three models; assume_single_clock states that rather than leaving it implicit.
